premise: claymation. a bakery at dawn, the baker is my grandmother
scenes: In a cozy claymation kitchen powdered with flour, grandmother pulls a tray of golden croissants from the oven with a warm, wrinkled smile. As she sets the hot tray right in front of you, one of the clay pastries suddenly blinks, wiggles its crescent tips, and lets out a tiny yawn.

Grandmother is humming softly in the dawn light of the claymation bakery, using a wooden spoon to blend a vibrant, swirling batter that glows with impossible neon colors. She winks, scoops up a heaping dollop of the glowing mixture, and holds the spoon inches from your mouth just as the batter begins to emit a high-pitched radio broadcast.

Through the frosted windows of the claymation bakery, the morning sun catches grandmother as she kneads an enormous, groaning mound of dough on the butcher block. Without warning, the elastic clay dough snaps outward, instantly enveloping both of her arms and pinning her against the counter while the door chime rings to announce the first customer of the day.
prompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Claymation, first-person POV at eye level, one continuous shot, natural head sway, no cuts. The flour-dusted wooden countertop stretches forward, holding a black metal baking sheet full of golden, bumpy clay croissants. Standing across the counter, grandmother, a clay figure with textured grey hair tied in a bun, wire-rimmed glasses, and a blue calico apron, beams warmly. In the center of the tray, one curved pastry opens two dark bead eyes, flexing its crescent ends like small arms and parting a seam along its flaky body with a squeaky peep. Grandmother's smile vanishes, her sculpted mouth dropping into a small round circle behind her glasses. A right hand sculpted from pale clay extends from the bottom of the frame toward the living pastry. The croissant snaps its doughy body upward, leaping off the tray directly toward the camera with tiny clay teeth bared inside its split seam.

overall_soundscape: Soft humming of an old oven cooling down, a tiny high-pitched pastry yawn and squeak, grandmother's sharp intake of breath, the metallic scrape of the baking tray, and a sudden wet clay slap as the pastry springs forward.

non_diegetic_music: None.
notes: all three scenes say claymation and keep grandmother. The style rule reached the prompt ('Claymation, first-person POV'); the writer made the hand 'sculpted from pale clay' on its own. Every scene goes surreal (living croissant, glowing radio batter, dough that pins her); the premise didn't ask for surreal.
